approved: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 5) Bill 2015

The speaker argued against higher taxes and for more responsible spending, noting Australia's $30 billion deficit and $154 billion welfare bill, and opposed a change to car expense claims that would cost rural businesses around $500 in deductions.

Labor supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 5) Bill 2015, which saves $1.4 billion over forward estimates by reforming work-related car expenses, zone tax offset, salary packaged entertainment benefits, and third-party reporting to the ATO. The speaker argued the government's "spending problem" narrative is false, citing high tax-to-GDP ratios and opposition to a regressive GST increase that would hurt low-income earners.

Supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment Bill 2015 for modernising tax collection and streamlining processes, and criticised the member for Fraser's amendment and Labor's failure to restrain expenditure growth.

The bill amends tax laws to modernise work-related car expense deductions (abolishing two outdated methods, introducing a single 66c per km rate, raising $845 million), tighten the zone tax offset by excluding fly-in fly-out workers ($325 million), cap uncapped entertainment benefits for not-for-profit employees at $5,000, and create a third-party reporting regime for specified transactions.
Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 5) Act 2015
